text: Every language starts here. Python's version of variables and data types is refreshingly simple, and it's the absolute foundation for everything else in this chapter.
No declaration keyword, no upfront type. Just a name, an equals sign, a value. Python figures out the type from the value itself — that's called dynamic typing.

Five core types you'll use constantly, mapped to real taxi columns. Fare amount is a float. Passenger count is an int. Vendor ID — even though it looks numeric — is actually stored as text, a string. A shared ride flag is a boolean, true or false. And a genuinely missing value is None.
When something behaves unexpectedly, type of tells you exactly what Python decided a value's type actually is. You'll reach for this constantly once you start reading real files in Lesson 22.

And remember: None means genuinely absent, not zero, not an empty string. Confusing those is a real, common bug. Next lesson: lists and dictionaries, for holding more than one value at a time. See you there.
